interest: This file is valuable for labor and legal historians as it documents the institutionalization of Japan's distinctive system of retirement and dismissal allowances during the 1930s, tracing its transition from customary commercial practice to codified statutory law under Law No. 42 of 1936. It uniquely reveals how practical commercial dilemmas encountered by American enterprises operating in Japan—specifically legal and customary severance liabilities toward long-term Japanese employees upon corporate liquidation—directly motivated U.S. diplomatic inquiries and reporting. Furthermore, the docket sheet illustrates the information-gathering network connecting private American law firms, the Department of State, and consular officers in Tokyo who analyzed Japanese socioeconomic legislation and employment customs in the prewar period.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.5044) consists of a two-page 'List of Papers' docket sheet recording official correspondence, despatches, and inquiries between 1930 and 1936 regarding Japanese labor conditions and employer-employee relations, specifically the customs and legal regulations governing retirement and dismissal allowances. The file indexes an initial 1930 cross-reference to an embassy report by William R. Castle, Jr., followed by a 1933 voluntary report on dismissal allowances by Consul General Arthur Garrels. In 1934, the Chicago law firm Scott, MacLeish & Falk, represented by Leland K. Neeves, sought State Department guidance on Japanese retirement allowance obligations on behalf of a client terminating a 25-year Japanese employee due to business closure. This inquiry prompted instructions to the American consulate general in Tokyo, where Consul Addison E. Chapman prepared a detailed January 1935 report on the legal status and calculation of severance pay in Japan. The file concludes with a September 1936 despatch from Edwin L. Neville enclosing an English translation of Japan's newly promulgated Law No. 42 of June 2, 1936, which legally mandated retirement reserve funds and retirement allowances.

subfiles.summary: This document constitutes the official State Department docket sheet for decimal file 894.5044, indexing records relating to Japanese labor relations and retirement allowances between 1930 and 1936. It records an initial 1930 cross-reference to an embassy report by William R. Castle, Jr., a 1933 voluntary report by Consul General Arthur Garrels, and a 1934–1935 exchange with Chicago attorney Leland K. Neeves regarding the customary and legal rights of Japanese employees to severance pay upon business discontinuance. The list further details consular investigations in Tokyo led by Addison E. Chapman that culminated in a January 1935 report on retirement allowance calculations, and concludes with a September 1936 despatch from Edwin L. Neville enclosing the text of Japan's Law No. 42 regarding retirement reserves.
